scenes.b: Despite all this wisdom… why is my heart not at peace? That question of Sage Vyasa — is the root of this story.
The answer came from Sage Narada — let the story of devotion be your pen; the Lord's glory must be your composition.
Those very words became his anchor. Now, only a moment — the threshold before a great valley.
That night, the ashrama waited in silence — as if something great was about to happen.
The river kept speaking on its endless journey. The mountains stood as silent witnesses.
The moment just before dawn — darkness melts, and a thought is born.
The first ray touched the ashrama. A morning ready for change.
The night's contemplation had settled beside those very pages. Today, the pen must be born anew.
Vyasa rose — without fatigue. The smile he had worn all night was still with him.
The disciples went about their duties. The ashrama is waking — morning is complete.
He looked toward the east. Outside, the sun was rising — and inside, another.
Those eyes now shone with quiet resolve. What must be done — is known.
The disciples followed in silence — wherever the Guru walks, that path itself is their school.
Step by step, he reached the riverbank. When the goal is clear, the way appears of itself.
The Saraswati flowed without fear. Far away, blue mountains — an infinite, beautiful expanse.
A lone crane stood at the water's edge — it too a meditator: gaze in the water, stillness in the mind.
As the Guru asked for his seat — both disciples' hands reached the mat at once. Even rivalry in devotion is nature.
He sat upon the flat stone — the water's voice, the wind's pace, the sun's angle… everything was right.
Achamana — a palmful of water. With it, not only the hands but the mind is purified.
What he took, he offered back. Gratitude is his tradition — never take from the world on loan.
He spread the seat, set the mala, placed the water pot beside. Meditation is the greatest invitation — all else is small.
The disciples stood apart. Some journeys belong to the Guru alone — their waiting itself is service.
The wind let fall a single leaf — the river received it in silence. To flow on simply is also meditation.
His spine rose straight; his mind grew still. He will remain — until the inner self calls.
Narada's blessing returned — that hand upon his head, those words in his chest: let devotion's story be your pen.
One last look east — then he closed his eyes. Meditation had begun.
His breath slowed. The mala in his hand stopped. Every sound was drifting away.
Ready to release the world. Within — a circle of light began to open.
All things melted into golden radiance. No fear — only endless peace.
Only the tilak remained — the open door to the inner world.
The inner sky — without limits. Amidst star-dust, silent peace spread wide.
There… a point of light seemed to float. From an unseen direction, that light kept growing.
The light kept growing — a sunrise within the heart. A lamp lit nowhere outside began to glow within.
The river of the heart dissolved into an ocean of light. The final boundary was gone.
Like the ocean of milk — a sea of golden light. Nothing here but infinite peace.
Upon that sea floated a luminous form — lotus, conch, discus, mace… the divine form shining forth.
That face — compassion given form. Whoever beholds it knows no fear; only love remains.
Within the light, Narada's words echoed — reach Him through devotion; that is your peace, that is your story.
His rays reached every direction — no place without light, no heart they could not touch.
Vyasa's inner light — a small point now — bowed before that great form. The offering was complete.
The blessing rained down as golden wings — a rain of light. To whoever asks, giving is His nature.
Beside His feet danced a consciousness like a transparent veil. Its name — Maya. Beautiful, enchanting.
Maya tried to cover the light — but it slipped past her and flowed on with ease.
Maya danced on — half shadow, half light. She too is His power; only in His presence does she dance.
Some souls seemed to forget beneath that veil — their glow had grown a little dim.
Maya too is His power. The veil cannot tear itself — but with devotion, His grace parts it gently.
From that ocean rose countless golden flames — the souls. No two alike, yet the journey is one.
Each flame walks holding its slender thread — each journey its own, each karma its own.
The flames joined and became constellations — no one is alone. Bonding is the language of creation.
In one flame a child's smile, in another a mother's face, in another a farmer's hands — all of life was in them.
All the threads arrived at last into His hands — gentle as fingers upon a flute's strings.
The constellation slowly took the shape of a great lotus — creation's secret form, a luminous order of devotion.
From those flames toward Him — a golden path had formed. Its name: bhakti.
Along that path, the holy names rang like bells. Sound itself became light — kirtan became a lamp.
Narada's words resonated like a celestial veena — where bhakti is born, knowledge moves, and peace resides.
Some flames reached Him step by step along that path — bliss… indescribable bliss.
The Lord, Maya, the souls, the path of devotion — one great mandala. The vision complete; the duty to preserve it in words, now his.
That mandala — reflected into a drop of ink. The vision had to flow into words. The Bhagavatam… ready to move.
Breath returned. Eyelids stirred softly. The world was his again — but he had changed.
He opened his eyes — no confusion, no doubt. Only clarity. The divine truth rested within him.
The river flowed more peacefully than before. In its waters his smile shimmered — a smile to wonder the world.
The disciples came near with reverence. A new radiance on the Guru's face — visible to all.
One whispered to another: a sunrise has happened upon Gurudev's face — and the smile reached everyone.
He walked back to the ashrama — a new resolve in his stride. What is received is taken only to be shared.
Palm leaves were spread. Ink, stylus, lamp — all was ready for the composition. A new morning for a new scripture.
The stylus dipped into ink. The first line was written — the first step of a story that will stand for ages.
Upon the palm leaf, golden letters stood shining. Not mere writing — a nectar-stream of devotion. Srimad Bhagavatam — now it begins.
Srimad Bhagavatam — this divine journey is about to begin. Subscribe — so every story of devotion reaches you.
